plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09): modelling situations involving earning money and budgeting, asking 'Can I afford it?' and 'Do I need it?'
plan.shape: example-first with a weekly budget table, because income, expenses and money left over are new words for many
plan.criticalFeature: money left over = income minus all the expenses
decisionPoints: the choice check: which is an expense?
the hinge: can Leo afford the game this week?
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation
plan.catchUp: Missed last week? Show one change-from-a-purchase problem with the plan frame before the launch.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Sort income and expenses, read Ava's week, a budget table, a mistake, and can I afford it?
resources.title: Earning and Spending
resources.subtitle: Money left over = income minus all the expenses.

example.prompt: Is 'a $10 birthday gift' income or an expense?
steps: An expense is money going out.

items.prompt: Sort each money event for a Year 6 student.
Ava earned $20 pocket money and $15 mowing. She spent $8.50 at the canteen, $6 on bus fares and $12.50 at the movies.
Fill the gaps in this weekly budget.

example.prompt: Mia has $8 left over each week. Can she afford a $25 game after 3 weeks?

items.prompt: Jai earns $18 a week and spends $11.50. Can he afford $30 footy boots after 5 weeks? Explain.
items.answer: Left over $6.50 a week; 5 × $6.50 = $32.50, so yes, with $2.50 spare.

items.prompt: Zara worked out her money left over. Find her mistake and fix it.
items.answer: She only took off one expense. Expenses total $27.50, so $40 - $27.50 = $12.50 left over.

items.prompt: Sam can afford a $60 skateboard, but he already has one. What is the best question to ask first?
items.explain: Being able to afford something does not mean you need it. Asking 'Do I need it?' helps you save for things that matter more.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. A monthly budget, percentage of income spent, and planning a wants and needs list, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Budget Planner
resources.subtitle: Plan a month. Find the percentage spent.

example.prompt: Earn $15 a week for 4 weeks, spend $40. Left over?

items.prompt: Lily earns $22.50 a week. Complete her 4-week budget.
In which week did Lily have the most left over? What fraction of that week's income did she keep?
Lily wants a $45 jacket. If weeks 1 to 4 repeat, after how many weeks can she buy it?
items.answer: After 4 weeks she has $25.55; after week 7 she has $25.55 + $8.50 + $2.75 + $14.30 = $51.10, so 7 weeks

example.prompt: Income $40, spent $30. What percentage was spent?

items.prompt: Income $50, spent $35. What percentage was spent? What percentage was saved?
Ben spends 85% of his $60. Tom spends $48 of his $64. Who saves a bigger percentage? Explain.
items.answer: Ben saves 15%; Tom spends 75%, saves 25%. Tom saves a bigger percentage.

example.prompt: Is lunch a need or a want?
steps: You must eat to be healthy.
Lunch is a need (a fancy lunch might be a want).

items.prompt: Make a list of 5 needs and 5 wants for a Year 6 student. Then plan a $50 budget that covers the needs first. Show the costs and what is left.
items.answer: Check: needs are covered first, costs add up correctly, and the total is $50 or less.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: whole-dollar amounts, one expense at a time, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Budget: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: In minus out = left over.

items.prompt: Buying a drink: in or out?
items.hint: Do you get money or spend it?

items.prompt: Washing the car for $5: in or out?
items.hint: Do you get money or spend it?

slides.notes: Session 1 of our budgeting week: today we work out income, expenses and money left over.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk; calculators are optional for checking. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Sale price
prompts: A $70 jacket is 20% off. What is the sale price?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with last week's money maths.
ASK: What is the sale price of a 70 dollar jacket at 20 percent off?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $56
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> find 10 percent, double it, then take it off. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 20 percent of 70 is 14 off,
so you pay 56 dollars. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing $14, the discount.
Fix: ask what you pay, and they subtract.
notes.prep: Review of last week's modelling with percentages (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What does a 36 dollar game cost with GST?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $39.60
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> find 10 percent, 3.60, then add it on. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent of 36 is 3.60, so 39.60 dollars. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing $32.40.
Fix: say GST is added on, and they add.

beats: ASK: Which is the better buy: 5 for 8 dollars, or 8 for 12 dollars?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 8 for $12
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> find the price of one in each together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 5 for 8 is 1.60 each, and 8 for 12 is 1.50 each,
so 8 for 12 is the better buy. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing 5 for $8 because it costs less.
Fix: find the price for one in each, and they compare.

beats: SAY: Now for our nine times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 9 times 6?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 54
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 sixes is 60, take one 6 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 54. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 56 or 45.
Fix: 10 sixes is 60, take away 6, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 9 times 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 72
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 eights is 80, take one 8 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 72. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 81 or 63.
Fix: 10 eights is 80, take away 8, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many nines make 63?
ASK: What is 63 divided by 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in nines to 63. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 7. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 6 or 8.
Fix: check: 7 nines is 63, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to work out income, expenses and money left over.
successCriteria: I can sort money into income and expenses.
I can work out the money left over in a budget.
I can decide whether I can afford something, and whether I need it.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week is about earning, saving and budgeting.
Today we track money coming in and going out.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 sorting is reachable for everyone; SC2 money left over is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 afford and need is the stretch.

slides.title: Where does the money go?
slides.prompt: Leo had $40 this week. What did he spend most on?

beats: POINT to the graph.
SAY: Leo got 40 dollars this week. This graph shows where it went.
ASK: What did Leo spend most on, and how much did he save?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: fun, $15; saved $7
SCAN boards for fun and 7.
80%+ -> cold call one student: Is that a good way to use $40? Why?
Less -> lay a ruler across each column top together. Re-ask.
SAY: Fun was the biggest, at 15 dollars, and he saved 7.
Today we track money coming in and going out,
so we can make choices like Leo's.
trap: reading the scale wrongly.
Fix: lay a ruler across the column top, and they read again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: a real week of money. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: Money you spend: money going out.
slides.example: Bus fares and canteen lunches are expenses.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is expense. Say it with me: ex-pense.
SAY: An expense is money you spend, money going out.
Its partner is income: money coming in.
ASK: Is pocket money income or an expense?
Show one finger for income, two for expense.
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: one finger: income
trap: calling pocket money an expense.
Fix: ask whether it comes in or goes out, and they decide again.
notes.prep: Income and expense are the two sides of every budget.

beats: MODEL adding the income.
SAY: Ava's money coming in is 20 dollars
pocket money and 15 for mowing: 35 dollars.
MODEL adding the expenses.
SAY: Going out: 8.50, 6 and 12.50. That's 27 dollars of expenses.
ASK: So how much money does Ava have left over?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $8
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 35 take away 27 is 8 dollars left over.
That's what she could save this week.
trap: taking off only one expense.
Fix: add all the expenses first, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: What percentage of her income did Ava spend?
notes.help: Circle the ins in one colour and the outs in another.
notes.prep: Left over = income minus all expenses: the critical feature. SC2.

slides.title: Can I afford it? Do I need it?
steps: A $34 game: $36 is enough, so he can afford it.
Do I need it? Think before buying.

notes.answer: yes after 4 weeks; need is a choice
beats: POINT to the table.
SAY: Leo has 9 dollars left over each week,
and he wants a 34 dollar game.
MODEL checking each week.
SAY: After 3 weeks he has 27, not enough.
After 4 weeks, 36: he can afford it.
But there's a second question: do I need it?
ASK: Leo hasn't finished his last game. Should he buy it? Tell your partner.
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: a reason to wait or to buy
REVEAL after partners have shared.
SAY: He can afford it after 4 weeks, with 2 dollars spare.
Whether he should is his choice.
trap: saying yes after 3 weeks.
Fix: check 27 against 34, and they recount.
notes.help: Keep a running total each week.
notes.prep: Afford and need are different questions. SC3.

slides.title: Which is an expense?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: thinks any money activity is spending
confuses money coming in with money going out

beats: SAY: Think: does the money come in, or go out?
ASK: Which one is an expense?
10 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What are A and C?
Less -> act it out: hold out a hand for in,
give a coin away for out. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B: buying a ticket is money going out.
A and C both bring money in, so they're income.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: ask whether you get money or spend it at a stall,
and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point: income versus expense.

slides.title: Money left over
slides.ask: How much money is left over?
slides.pivot: add all the expenses first, then take them from the income
slides.followUp: cold call one board: What were the total expenses?

items.say: Nothing left over: the expenses add to exactly 50 dollars.

say: Write the money left over on your board.
trap: taking off only one expense.
Fix: add all the expenses first, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Find the percentage left over for each one.
notes.help: Circle the income, box the expenses.
notes.prep: Guided practice from two expenses to decimals and a zero left over. SC2.

slides.title: Can Leo afford it this week?
slides.label: He wants a $16 game.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Find his money left over, then decide.
ASK: Can Leo afford the 16 dollar game this week? How much would be left?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: yes, $1.50 left
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> add income, add expenses, subtract, together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Income 35, expenses 17.50, so 17.50 left.
Yes, he can afford it, with 1.50 spare. Tick it or fix it.
trap: forgetting the odd jobs income.
Fix: circle every income line, and they redo it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone saying no, or using one expense, starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Work out income, expenses and money left over on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Have you included every expense?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: missing an income or expense line.
Fix: tick each line as they use it, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: a monthly budget, percentage spent, and needs and wants.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: whole-dollar amounts, one expense at a time.
notes.prep: Independent practice: sorting, a weekly budget, afford and need, and a mistake. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: What does Mia have left at the end of her week?

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What does Mia have left at the end of her week?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $17.75
RECORD who leaves out a line or subtracts one expense.
They start tomorrow's saving plan with the teacher.
trap: writing $27.50.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new budget with decimals.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner the two questions to ask before buying something.

notes.answer: open - listen for can I afford it, and do I need it?
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can work out money left over?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with $27.50 on the board matters most.
ASK: What two questions should you ask before you buy something?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: can I afford it, and do I need it?
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: saving plans.
